stops.label: Selected Thomas sayings supply concrete comparison points. Priesthood is examined through functions and qualifications, not names alone.

stops.title: Preservation is not the same as origin
stops.label: Enochic and Nag Hammadi reception opens a wider map, while proposed institutional carriers remain separately inspectable.

trails.title: Inheritance, judgment and repair
trails.question: How does an inherited source become an argument about authority and restoration?

stops.title: Who can authorize release?
stops.label: Follow the completed Melchizedek comparison from inherited roles to different grounds of authority.

stops.title: Do not date a text from its emotion
stops.label: The requested cross-corpus study will separate independently argued dates from descriptions of anger, resistance and repair.

stops.title: What should the next conscious beings inherit?
stops.label: The constructive theology asks how an inward standard can correct desire and how repair can avoid reproducing domination.

trails.title: How an inward model acquires a history
trails.question: How do teachings, communities, copies and ritual settings participate in formation?

stops.title: An inward covenant
stops.label: Inward instruction and renewal occur within Israel/Judah restoration settings. Work-level dates remain open.

stops.title: Formation through a community
stops.label: Compare admission, conduct and liturgical participation. A physical copy is not the composition date or proof of a later institutional route.

stops.title: Christ formed, and the surviving witness
stops.label: The Pauline passages and the P46 collection witness have different roles. The selected Michigan image shows Hebrews, not Galatians 4:19.

stops.title: Interpretation that changes the receiver
stops.label: Compare interpretive knowledge, priestly authority and recurrent self-formation without collapsing them into one doctrine.

stops.title: An embodied setting and two interpretations
stops.label: The font and painted setting are material evidence. Domestic continuity, architectural differentiation and construction dates remain separately inspectable interpretations.

trails.title: A world, a mind and a proposed ground
trails.question: What changes when physical reality is interpreted as an expression within divine reality?

stops.title: A representation is not its referent
stops.label: Begin with the full cosmic argument, then distinguish a generated experience from an externally created object.

stops.title: Necessity and selection
stops.label: Inspect the move from contingency to a necessary ground, then the further argument for agency.

stops.title: One word, several measures
stops.label: Neural coherence, integration and quantum coherence do not become identical merely by sharing a name.

stops.title: The self that can be corrected
stops.label: Follow the inward model into choices and repair, without making computation alone a moral standard.

trails.title: The flood and the inheritance it carries
trails.question: How can a tradition preserve a narrative while changing what its survival means?

stops.title: Before the ancestral beginning
stops.label: Read the Sumerian comparison and Genesis without treating Abraham as the beginning of every inherited story.

stops.title: An object with its own date
stops.label: The seventh-century attribution belongs to K.3375, not to the flood or the first telling of the story.

stops.title: What changes when the roles merge?
stops.label: Compare the organization of judgment, rescue and responsibility rather than only names.

stops.title: A chronology needs endpoints
stops.label: Connect the flood comparison to departure and sanctuary while keeping each source count explicit.

trails.title: The Teacher and prophetic time
trails.question: Which event does a sacred count identify: appearance, death or restoration?

stops.title: The sequence before the name
stops.label: Seven weeks, 62 weeks and a final week must be assigned to events before a date can identify a person.

stops.title: The counted history
stops.label: 390 and 20 place the Teacher's appearance within the model. The extra 40-year career is a reconstruction, not a fourth explicit datum.

stops.title: What the count authorizes
stops.label: Release, forgiveness and anointed authority create a specific interpretive connection. Competing readings of damaged words change the sequence.

stops.title: Two versions must not be blended
stops.label: The illustrative 176 BCE appearance and the October 147-to-88 BCE reconstruction have different assumptions. Neither supplies an archaeological date.

stops.title: From sacred time to transmitted life
stops.label: A displaced-biography claim needs carriers of the founder's memory, not only a matching number. Follow the proposed Egyptian branch.

trails.title: Onias and the priestly branches
trails.question: How could a priestly inheritance persist across borders and after its sanctuary closes?

stops.title: An institution beyond Jerusalem
stops.label: Josephus supplies a reported sanctuary, priests and royal permission. The appeal to Isaiah explains a claim of continuity, not only a break.

stops.title: A named next generation
stops.label: Chelcias and Ananias appear as sons of the temple-founder. Their offices and cross-border counsel give the carrier question specific actors.

stops.title: Families and specialized groups
stops.label: A marrying Essene order and household rules complicate a uniform celibate picture. Neither is a roster of the proposed migration.

stops.title: The destination also closes
stops.label: The Egyptian sanctuary is not an indefinitely available refuge. Its reported closure makes surviving households and dispersed institutions a new research question.

stops.title: What changes, and what survives?
stops.label: Reunion, succession and transformed interpretation are the positive reconstruction. Texts, dates and actual intermediates must support each proposed connection.

trails.title: James: authority, family and knowledge
trails.question: What is transmitted when the founder is no longer present?

stops.title: A named teaching chain
stops.label: Compare the reported knowledge transmission with the leadership question, without treating one surviving host as many independent witnesses.

stops.title: A priestly portrait
stops.label: Ritual authority, holiness and genealogy are different possible explanations of the portrait.

stops.title: Succession and contested classification
stops.label: Family selection does not erase the account's classification of Essenes as opponents.

stops.title: Rival continuations
stops.label: External Ebionite reports preserve both useful affinities and differences that a transmission model must explain.

stops.title: An inheritance with several carriers
stops.label: Read the complete proposed history of leadership, households and transmitted teaching.

trails.title: Thomas: reading, formation and carriers
trails.question: What changes in a copied text, and what changes in its reader?

stops.title: Leadership and private understanding
stops.label: The comparison separates communal authority from an interpreter's encounter.

stops.title: An earlier reading of transformation
stops.label: Credit Owens's earlier comparison without confusing it with the stronger displaced-founder chronology.

stops.title: Partial witnesses
stops.label: A Greek fragment can attest its surviving sayings, not all the absent contents of a collection.

stops.title: A possible educational carrier
stops.label: The reported Greek James revelation suggests a teaching context. Its date belongs to the copy, and its image is not redistributed.

stops.title: From received words to an operative model
stops.label: Read the full historical argument alongside the modern constructive account, without treating one as proof of the other.
